description: Swiss Ephemeris .Net portage. SwissEphSharp is the package ID this project is distributed under: the continuation of Yan Grenier's SwissEphNet C# port, tracking Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.04. The assembly is now named SwissEphSharp too, so it can coexist with the original SwissEphNet package; the namespace stays SwissEphNet, so source that only uses the public API needs no changes beyond the PackageReference itself. Callers of the removed OnLoadFile event still need to migrate to SwissEph.FileProvider. Not published or endorsed by Yan Grenier or Astrodienst.
releaseNotes:
2.10.4.0:
- BREAKING: SE_FNAME_DFT2 is removed. Upstream deleted it together with the DE406 fallback in
  open_jpl_file, so code that names the constant no longer compiles. SE_FNAME_DFT is now
  de441.eph and SE_DE_NUMBER is 441. A caller that has only de431.eph must now call
  swe_set_jpl_file("de431.eph"). The changed values (SE_TIDAL_DEFAULT, SE_TIDAL_SWIEPH,
  SE_TIDAL_JPLEPH, SEMOD_DELTAT_DEFAULT, SEMOD_NDELTAT, SE_DE_NUMBER, SE_FNAME_DFT) are C#
  consts, so code compiled against 2.10.3.x keeps the old values until it is recompiled.
- Results move without a code change. The default Delta T model is now
  SEMOD_DELTAT_STEPHENSON_ETC_2020 (new, model 6), the Morrison, Stephenson, Hohenkerk and
  Zawilski 2021 spline, used before 1 January 1962; dt[] runs to 2033 and adjust_for_tidacc()
  changed. UT-input results before 1962 and after 2020 differ from 2.10.3.3. Measured from the
  MSVC-built C, swe_deltat_ex at JD 2086302.5 (1 January 1000 proleptic Gregorian, 27 December 999
  Julian) is 0.018871612655972776 days under model 6 and 0.016726901931961108 days under model 5,
  the former default: 185.303 s apart.
  SE_TIDAL_DEFAULT is SE_TIDAL_DE441 (was SE_TIDAL_DE431) and SE_TIDAL_STEPHENSON_2020 is new.
- With SEFLG_HELCTR the second light-time pass uses the heliocentric distance (upstream 8178d0ac;
  upstream's figures: Mars in 2016 by 21 mas, Mercury up to 0.84 arcseconds).
- swe_calc chooses the ephemeris file by the date of the call, so results at file boundaries no
  longer depend on call history (upstream 79d3553f, 85eb3a5d). When the light-time point falls
  outside the JPL file, the Moon falls back to Moshier.
- The Chiron, Pholus, interpolated-apsides and file-limit messages now give the JD and the calendar
  date, for example "Chiron not available at JD 1967600.5 = 31.12.0674j; restricted to JD
  1967601.5 = 01.01.0675j - JD 3419437.5 = 01.01.4650". swetest -lim prints JD and -fT dates and
  shows the errors of the interpolated apsides.
- swe_set_astro_models("") selects the current version's models. SEFLG_JPLHOR without the JPL file
  returns a warning in serr. load_dpsi_deps reads the EOP dpsi column at the corrected offsets and
  swe_close resets the EOP state. Upstream's sepl, semo and seas files were regenerated on DE441;
  take the v2.10.04 files if you rely on the ephemeris data.
- Port fix: swed is now cleared in place on first initialisation, as sweph.c:1257 does. On a fresh
  SwissEph, swe_get_astro_models("SE2.06") listed the default models where the C gives "-amod5,...",
  and swe_nod_aps returned wrong apsides for some bodies and dates (Sun MEAN at JD 1000000:
  perihelion 215.299, the C gives 302.338). This predates the sync.
- Also in this release, merged since 2.10.3.3: read_const no longer drops leading digits of an
  asteroid's name beyond the C's prefix scan; the SEFLG_SIDEREAL Moshier-fallback warning is no
  longer erased by plaus_iflag; a planet file opened as an asteroid file returns an error instead
  of throwing; a seorbel.txt line with a trailing comma is accepted; swetest strcat slips,
  FormatToDegreeMinuteSecond rounding, C.sprintf signs and non-finite values, non-seekable file
  streams, and double-to-int conversions on .NET 9 and later are fixed; fixed-star loading is
  faster. See CHANGELOG.md for each.
- The upstream pin moves from 43c9fe54 to the tag v2.10.04 (e308765d10b9463ab0ed53b102ad454820ee0b43),
  the first upstream tag since v2.10.3bfinal. SE_VERSION is "2.10.04".
- Verification against the MSVC-built C at e308765d: both oracle grids are bit-identical (27,437
  analytic and 3,376 file rows) with empty known-diff lists; 251 of 268 swetest cases are
  byte-identical and the other 17 differ only by the directory separator and -nan(ind). The
  conformance corpus is now 11 suites and 18,919 iterations; known-fail.tsv has 1,401 rows (all
  VALUE-MISMATCH, down from 2,395; the harness no longer skips iterations for want of data and the
  DATA-MISSING category is gone), and all 1,401 are triaged against the C as drift, none a port
  defect; each is also pinned field by field in known-fail-pins.tsv. The 972 house-speed rows of 2.10.3.3 pass against
  the regenerated t.exp.
- Known issues: v2.10.04's dt[] has 69.2093 for 2023 where USNO's deltat.data has 69.2039, and the
  prediction 69.05 for 2026.0 where the measured value is 69.1099; the port keeps the C's values and
  a correction is being prepared for upstream. Upstream's setest harness (not the library)
  declares undersized arrays in suite_09_rise.c and aborts under gcc's stack protector at 9.2.9.
  See docs/known-issues.md.

2.10.3.3:
- House cusp speeds are now analytic for every house system. swe_houses_ex2 and
  swe_houses_armc_ex2 (and the older entry points that forward to them) previously used a
  finite-difference interpolation that returned values in the millions of degrees per day near the
  Ascendant's horizon tangency (ARMC 90 and 270); it now runs only as a fallback when an analytic
  result is not finite. This is the eleven-patch house cusp-speed set that Timothy van der Ham
  reported to the Swiss Ephemeris mailing list in August 2026 and that Astrodienst applied
  upstream in commit 6c989727. Behaviour change for callers that read cusp or ascmc speeds. By
  system: P and G implicit function theorem; K chain rule through the MC (the old value was up to
  39% high at latitude 60); O cusps 11 and 12 from the MC speed instead of the Ascendant speed
  (34-38% shift); L, S and Q chain rule through the quadrant; X, M, F, B, U and Y closed form; I
  and i closed form with the Sun's declination held fixed (the omitted term reaches about 0.14
  degrees per day at latitude 35 and 0.6 at 52); W and N speeds are 0.
- Sidereal house speeds now account for the ayanamsa's rate: in the traditional sidereal mode it
  is subtracted from cusp and ascmc speeds (not from the ARMC, ascmc[2], and not from W and N cusps).
  Measured with swetest -b1.1.2000 -ut12:00 -house13.4,52.5,P -speed -sid1 -p0, the Ascendant
  moves at 600°43'39.3962 per day against 600°43'39.5410 tropical, 0.1448" less. With whole-sign
  houses every cusp speed is 0. ECL_T0 and SSY_PLANE modes subtract their auxiliary frame's rates
  (about 4e-5 degrees per day).
- SEFLG_RADIANS: house speeds are now converted to radians per day as well (they were left in
  degrees per day beside positions in radians).
- Three house position fixes: Y (APC) uses sin(kv) instead of the dasc round trip, so within 1e-10
  degrees of the equator cusps 1 and 7 are the Ascendant and Descendant (latitude 5e-11, ARMC 242:
  cusp 1 was 303.139, now 329.906); i (Makransky Sunshine) fixes w == 180 exactly and southern
  w == 90 or 270, and returns no cusp of exactly 360; G (Gauquelin) in the polar Porphyry
  fallback returns 0 for cusps 13 to 36 and their speeds (uninitialised in the C). I (Sunshine)
  declination error path returns ERR with all output arrays zeroed. swe_house_pos is unchanged.
- ECL_T0 sidereal modes near the mode's epoch t0: the frame rate is taken on tjde's side of t0
  when a central difference would straddle it (upstream 0c3eb56e). The cusps jump at t0 by twice
  the nutation in longitude, as in every earlier release; the first version of the frame-rate
  code (6c989727, never part of a SwissEphNet release) differenced across that jump and was off
  by up to 0.04 degrees per day within 0.1 day of t0. Measured for swetest -b1.1.2000 -ut12:00
  -house13.4,52.5,P -speed -sid18, the Ascendant's speed is 600°43'39.6898 against 600°43'39.5410
  tropical: the 0.149" difference is the frame term. The position jump at t0 is unchanged;
  SE_SIDBIT_SSY_PLANE is not affected.
- swe_calc on an asteroid (or other) ephemeris file at exactly the file's last date returned
  garbage: get_new_segment() took the index entry after the last segment. It now uses the last
  segment (upstream 43c9fe54; the port had the identical bug). Astraea (se00005s.se1) at exactly
  JD 2488932.5 came out at longitude 126.0072799, distance 3.648274082 au instead of 66.9437422
  and 3.288141871. It shows only when the last date is the first one evaluated, because an
  earlier date in the last segment caches that segment. New test AsteroidFileUpperLimitTest
  matches the MSVC-built C at 43c9fe54 bit for bit.
- swe_houses_armc_ex2 no longer raises SwissEph.OnTrace messages. Upstream removed the TRACE
  blocks from swehouse.c (6318ad4c); TRACE is defined by default in the .NET build, so the port's
  swe_houses_armc_ex2 raised them. Other OnTrace sources are unchanged.
- swe_get_planet_name now looks numbered asteroids up in seasnam.txt by binary search, which is
  faster; results are the same for a sorted file, and an unsorted file falls back to the full
  scan (sweph.c:6954, :6968).
- Programs/SweTest: -astpos now passes the ephemeris time te to print_asteroids (swetest.c:1613;
  the port had passed tjd since 2.10.3.2), and swe_get_planet_name is called only when the name is
  printed. This affects the SweTest program, not the library API.
- Swiss Ephemeris Professional License: the contract PDF was updated on 9 November 2026 ("Edition
  September 2026 update 9 Nov 2026",
  https://github.com/aloistr/swisseph/blob/6c9897279736b76e81f0b0039d05283a9ba59dc5/doc/secont_e_2609.pdf).
  The one substantive change is a new clause 13, "Use of language bindings and ports": every
  binding or port must honour the dual licensing (AGPL and Astrodienst's professional license),
  authors of bindings and ports may charge no extra fees, and Astrodienst lists the bindings it
  knows meet this. SwissEphNet is not in that list. SwissEphNet is already offered under both
  the AGPL-3.0 and the Professional License, as the README says, and this repository's LICENSE is
  unchanged. If you hold or plan to buy a Professional License, check the current contract with
  Astrodienst.
- The upstream pin moves from 94621aba to 43c9fe54 (upstream master), which is v2.10.3bfinal plus
  25 commits; no newer tag exists. SE_VERSION is still "2.10.03". 94621aba..43c9fe54 touches
  swehouse.c, sweph.c, swetest.c, ephe/seasnam.txt, ephe/seorbel.txt, ephe/astlistn.md, the
  contract PDF and bin/swetest (a prebuilt binary, nothing to port); the first three are ported
  above.
- Verification: the port is bit-exact against the MSVC-built C at 43c9fe54 on the oracle grids
  (27,437 analytic and 3,376 file rows). The characterization baseline was regenerated
  deliberately for the house-speed set, and passes unchanged at 43c9fe54. known-fail.tsv grows from 1,423 to 2,395
  rows, unchanged at 43c9fe54; the 972 new rows are setest 6.8 and 6.9 speed fields where t.exp's
  own values differ from the C's (positions unchanged), each with per-row evidence in docs and
  tests, not port defects. Unit tests: 354 of 354. No API change. See docs/known-issues.md for the detail.
- #47 added a DATA-MISSING triage file, XML documentation for the SE_SIDM_* constants, and
  docs/sidereal-and-vedic.md; no code change.

2.10.3.1:
- Full XML documentation (<summary>, <param>, <returns>) added for all 116
  public swe_* methods in SwissEphNet/SwissEph.swephexp.h.cs, plus the SEFLG_*/SE_*/SEMOD_*
  constants they reference. Purely additive: no signature or behavior changed, and
  SwissEphNet/CPort/ is untouched. IntelliSense now shows the same documentation a C caller
  gets from swephexp.h instead of nothing (CS1591 is suppressed repo-wide, so this gap was
  previously silent).
- Programs/SweTest: fixed insert_gap_string_for_tabs's LEN_SOUT bound. It now counts bytes the
  way the C's strlen does, using native single-byte semantics on Windows (the narrow-argv code
  page) and UTF-8 elsewhere, instead of counting UTF-16 characters. Accented -g gap values no
  longer stop tab substitution one byte early. This affects the SweTest program's console
  output, not the SwissEphSharp library API.
- swe_houses_ex2 now re-reads sid_data after its SE_SIDM_FAGAN_BRADLEY fallback, matching the
  C's pointer semantics (swehouse.c:221). No input reachable through the public API changes
  value from this today; it closes an audited fidelity gap rather than fixing an observed bug.
- Test coverage: BaselineMatrix now exercises 7 more of the library's 107 public entry points,
  all 100% EXACT on both TFMs. A new NutationTableFidelityTest value-diffs the nutation
  coefficient table against upstream source instead of only checking its length.
- CI gained macOS legs on the baseline and conformance gates (report-only).
- No breaking changes. See docs/known-issues.md and docs/compliance-2.10.04.md for the
  verification detail behind this release.

2.10.3 (the first release published to nuget.org, under the SwissEphSharp
package ID):
- LICENSE CHANGE, read this before upgrading. 2.8.0.2 was distributed under the GNU General
  Public License version 2 or later. This release is under the Swiss Ephemeris dual license:
  the GNU Affero General Public License, or a Swiss Ephemeris Professional License bought from
  Astrodienst. The practical difference is the AGPL's network clause. Under GPL-2.0 you could
  run this library inside a web service and owe nobody source, because nothing was distributed.
  Under the AGPL, operating the service is itself the trigger, and users who reach it over a
  network can require the complete corresponding source of your whole service, not just this
  library. If that does not work for your project, the Professional License is the other arm.
  This follows Astrodienst's own relicensing of Swiss Ephemeris and applies to the C library
  just as much as to this port. LICENSE, agpl-3.0.txt and NOTICE ship at the package root.
- SE_VERSION now reports "2.10.03", matching the C library this port tracks (upstream tag
  v2.10.3bfinal). Every stage of the 2.10.03 delta has landed: the header/constants stage,
  swephlib.c, the ayanamsha machinery, sweph.c, swecl.c, swehouse.c and swetest.c.
- swe_houses, swe_houses_ex, swe_houses_armc, swe_house_pos and swe_house_name each gained an
  int hsys overload alongside the existing char hsys overload, matching upstream swephexp.h.
- New API surface: swe_houses_ex2, swe_houses_armc_ex2, swe_calc_pctr, swe_get_current_file_data.
- swe_lun_occult_when_glob and swe_lun_occult_when_loc each gained an Int32 backward overload, so
  SE_ECL_ONE_TRY can be OR-ed into that bitfield the way swephexp.h declares. The existing bool
  overload is unchanged and still binds; it can only pass 0 or 1, so it can never request the
  flag. Reflection that resolves either method by name alone now throws AmbiguousMatchException.
- OnLoadFile is gone; ephemeris files are read from disk by default through the new
  SwissEph.FileProvider (IEphemerisFileProvider).
- The assembly is now named SwissEphSharp (was SwissEphNet), so this package can coexist in one
  dependency graph with the original SwissEphNet 2.8.0.2 instead of silently colliding with it at
  build time and crashing at runtime. The namespace stays SwissEphNet.
- 2.10.3 is the only release that ships netstandard2.0, not the last of several. 2.8.0.2 shipped
  net40 and netstandard1.0 and never carried netstandard2.0, and net8.0 or later will be required
  from the next release on, so the window in which this library is reachable from .NET Framework
  is this one version. Consumers on .NET Framework 4.6.1+ can take 2.10.3 and should pin to it
  deliberately rather than expect it to persist. netstandard2.0 is a compatibility target,
  not a correctness one: measured on .NET Framework 4.8 and 4.6.2 against .NET 10, the same
  asset's swe_calc differs on 29 of 102 calls (34 bodies x 3 epochs; worst case SE_ADMETOS
  latitude speed, 2.28e-3 relative -- an absolute divergence of 1.4e-08 deg/day against a base
  value of about -6.1e-06), while net8.0 and net10.0 agree on all 102. The cause is .NET
  Framework's less accurate Math.Sin/Math.Cos/Math.Tan near quarter-turn boundaries, not this
  port; see the "V:2.10.3" section of README.md for the full measurement.
- Numerous port bug fixes surfaced by the 2.10.03 work, several of them upstream C bugs Astrodienst
  fixed between 2.08 and 2.10.03 that this port now also carries: swe_nod_aps/swe_nod_aps_ut
  returning all-zero nodes and apsides, an obliquity read that affected every SEFLG_SWIEPH
  position, eclipse magnitude and obscuration off by a factor of 100, and the swe_house_pos buffer
  that was one element short for Gauquelin houses. See docs/compliance-2.10.04.md for the
  verification numbers behind this release and docs/known-issues.md and the "V:2.10.3" section
  of README.md for the full list.

- You are also inheriting everything in CHANGELOG.md's 2.8.1.0 entry, even though no such
  package was ever published. On nuget.org the step is 2.8.0.2 straight to this release, so
  those changes arrive with it: DIR_GLUE went from '\' to '/' on every platform, which changes
  the asteroid file names a file provider is asked for; DefaultEncoding became UTF-8 explicitly
  rather than falling back to it when Windows-1252 could not be resolved; and C.strcmp,
  strncmp, strstr and strchr became ordinal instead of culture-sensitive, which affects
  fixed-star name search and sort under a non-invariant culture.

Full history, back to the 2.08 upgrade: CHANGELOG.md at
